content: Namo Ārya Lokeśvarāya!To those who are equal to the dust motes of the infinite realms of the Victors of the ten directions,Whose compassion, born of attachment to beings, is as profound as the ocean,Who are renowned as Avalokiteśvara, in whom all qualities are spontaneously perfected—To that Protector, like a mountain of jewels, whom we all ought to serve, I bow.Upon a disk of cooling rays, full and bright, in the center of a stainless, fresh lotus,You sit in the posture of equality, with two feet as pure as the petals of a lotus.You are like the full moon in the world, shining brilliantly in every direction;The moment one sees you, the torment of the heart is dispelled and joy flourishes everywhere.Though cool as the touch of snow, you burn the hosts of Māra all the more;Though you transcend all phenomena of conceptual signs, you appear in a mandala of manifold manifestations;Though you have crossed beyond existence, you always show yourself taking birth in the three realms;Those possessed of wisdom marvel at your conduct, which is just like an illusion.You follow in the wake of all aspects, like the mandala of the autumn sky,By constantly relying on you, fortunate beings find a ground of unwearied peace.You are the blazing sun that brings an end to the darkness of ignorance in the entire world,And you bear the mark of the hare, dispelling the torment that scorches the mind with hatred.You display the beauty of your face, a mandala like a fully blossomed puṇḍarīka,Possessing a youthful grace that is lovely to behold, white as a stainless conch or crystal.In the midst of vast clouds of inconceivable offerings, you shine, performing the playful dance of illusion,Resplendent in the center of an infinite retinue of Sugatas, Bodhisattvas, and wrathful hosts.All those tormented by hundreds of sufferings, fallen into states of extreme wretchedness—Caused by fire, rivers, evil destinies, the fears of kings, and so forth—You draw them forth with your continuous chain of light, like a moon washed clean,And firmly establish them in supreme bliss, fully endowed with divine splendor.Fragrant locks of hair bound upon your crown mingle with the light of the sky,And the Lord of Victors, Amitābha, graces your head as a crown of your lineage.From the tip of your right hand in the gesture of supreme generosity, white nectar drops,Falling eternally like glistening pearls to quell the torments of all hungry ghosts.Your pure, lovely body rests with a graceful posture, your left hand leaning toward your hip,Indra and other powerful beings bow to you, for you are the sovereign of all the world.Adorned with the mudrās of the wheel, lotus, arrow, and bow,You perfectly display your thousand arms, thousand eyes, and eleven beautiful faces.At times you manifest as the lion’s roar, the leader of the fierce nāgas, and elsewhere,You display many miraculous forms such as Amoghapāśa and Nīlakaṇṭha.Sometimes you appear as the wrathful king Hayagrīva, the subduer of obstacles, or Mahākāla,Yet though you show a fierce demeanor that makes the three worlds tremble, your heart never wavers from compassion.The vast world that follows the path of space has no end,Yet your emanations are as numerous as the beings within it.Though you manifest them extensively, you do not think even a hair-tip moves,For you possess no conceptual effort, like rain falling from storm clouds.You have entirely abandoned words that do not serve the benefit of beings in any way,And through the branches of your unceasing melody, which accords with each individual's mind,You teach the paths of Dharma that exceed the number of atoms in the ocean,So that whoever hears your speech comes to abide in the authentic state.Like the song of a lovely maiden competing with the music of a gandharva's lute,Though it is pleasing, it utterly destroys the desires of those attached to objects.Even as you utter deep sounds like thunder filling the sky,You reduce the suffering of those terrified by fear to nothing but a name.To perfectly liberate those in samsara from their ever-wavering births,You turn the wheel of Dharma, proclaiming the profound truth in all its aspects,As you perfectly embody the speech of all the Victors of the three times,You, the lord of unsurpassed wealth, are renowned as the guru of all the world.Though some beings, even when facing their own suffering, occasionally fall under the power of angerAnd seek to kill, you always regard all beings as your own children;Because you have long since abandoned even the slightest intention to cause harm,Even the love I have for myself cannot compare to the rain of compassion in your heart.Cool as water infused with camphor, sandalwood, uśīra, and the like,You gaze upon the six realms with a peaceful, unblinking, and steady eye;Your realization, in which all conceptual projections of experience subside into the dharmadhātu,Is forever embraced by supreme bliss; to you, who are beyond all wavering, I prostrate.Burning with flames that blaze in every direction, with gaping mouths and eyes red with rage,The executioners create terror all around; amidst the blazing molten copper,In the hot hells where they are cooked like grain, may you cool them with a rain of nectar,And protect those afflicted by the cold that splits flesh and bone with the touch of warmth.With bellies like mountains, constricted throats, and limbs as thin as blades of grass,Their parched bodies are covered in dust, and sparks fly from the friction of their joints;Even rivers dry up at their mere glance; they are perpetually exhausted;To these hungry ghosts tormented by hunger, grant a rain of nectar-like food and drink.Craving the desire for even a single morsel of food, for the sake of that petty pleasure,They abandon their own precious lives and cannot distinguish between what to adopt and what to discard;To these animals, so extremely unfortunate in their ugly shapes and colors,May you grant the swift attainment of virtuous mindfulness and a life sustained by happiness.Even the splendor of the King of Brahmās, resting in a palace of blazing jewels,Must decline through impermanence, and in the Unrelenting Hell, bones and marrow burn;Even the gods who play in gentle, pleasant groves and on soft, comfortable beds,Must drink and be dragged across the ground by sharp iron thorns.Even those in high positions will, in no long time, become servants fit to be trampled underfoot;This youthfulness too will quickly fade, just like the flowers at the end of autumn;This wealth too is certain to be cast aside by time, like the fleeting joy of borrowed ornaments;And my life too, like a flash of lightning, appears here for but a single instant.Because of the distance from what we once knew, called the beyond of this world,And because I wander alone in the dense darkness of that state,Deceived in my heart by the illusions of the afflictions in this fearsome cyclic existence,Please draw us, your followers, from this ocean of suffering with your hand of compassion.In this land encircled by a fence of snow mountains, the Buddha’s teachings still remain,Yet most practitioners, stripped of the robes of discipline, are naked and devoid of shame;They fawn upon householders, seeking their favor, and engage in deeds condemned by the holy.Alas, the sunlight of the holy Dharma is about to set behind the mountain peaks.Those with power, intent on their own desires, contend with one another and harm the lowly;The lowly are constantly oppressed and find it difficult even to obtain a meal of coarse food.Since the noble ones remain indifferent in such an unbearable age of decadence,What use is their former vow, and to whom shall the subjects turn for refuge?It is said that your name is blessed, so that whoever hears it finds their fears pacified,And that the merit of holding your name is equal to serving countless Buddhas;Relying on these truthful words of the sages, we pray to you with longing:O Protector, abandon your indifference and please save these wretched sentient beings.May all beings respectfully attend to the Three Jewels,And through faith in the law of karma and its fruits, always enter the path of Dharma.Through the immeasurable, peaceful and wrathful miraculous displays that suit their varied dispositions and capacities,May you connect to happiness those dear ones who have fallen into this perilous state of existence.May I, too, with great devotion, possess the stainless wisdom that discerns reality,And through weariness with cyclic existence and compassion, strive to act for the benefit of others in many lives.Having attained the great power of the perfections that cause all demonic forces to be vanquished,May you long protect the beings and the pure way of the Dharma of Tuṣita.Though my intelligence is low, by the power of the ocean of my mind surging upward,This garland of praise and lament, like the beautiful, white, frothing foam,May whoever reads, hears, or remembers it have their stains of sin purified,And may they be cared for by the supreme Victor, the noble Avalokiteśvara, in the realm of Potalaka.
